subject: Vocabulary
topic: Word Usage — Commonly Confused Pairs in Context (W10 B2)

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word:
The pollution from the factory will ___ the health of residents in the area.
questions.explanation: B is correct. AFFECT (verb) = to have an impact on something. EFFECT (noun) = the result or outcome. Here, the blank needs a verb: 'will ___ the health'. So 'affect' is correct. Trick: EFFECT can rarely be a verb (meaning 'to bring about', e.g. 'effect a change'), but in the context of health, 'affect' is the standard choice. 'Infect' is about disease transmission (not general impact).

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word:
The dog ___ down and refused to move from its spot under the tree.
questions.explanation: B is correct. LAY (past tense of 'lie' = to recline) is the correct choice: 'The dog lay down.' Principal parts: lie→lay→lain. Trap: 'Laid' is past tense of 'lay' (transitive: to put something), which needs an object: 'She laid the book down'. 'Lied' = told an untruth. 'Lain' = past participle of 'lie' (used with 'has/had': 'The dog had lain there').

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word:
There were ___ than twenty students who passed the entrance exam.
questions.explanation: B is correct. FEWER is used with countable nouns (students, books, people). LESS is used with uncountable/mass nouns (water, time, money). Since 'students' is countable, use 'fewer'. Golden rule: if you can count them individually, use 'fewer'. 'Less' students is a very common spoken error that SSC exploits in error-detection questions.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word:
The data from the survey allowed the researchers to ___ that people prefer quality over price.
questions.explanation: B is correct. INFER = to reach a conclusion from evidence (the researchers drew a conclusion from the data). IMPLY = to suggest something indirectly (the speaker/writer implies; the listener/reader infers). Memory aid: The DATA implies → the RESEARCHER infers. Here, the researchers are doing the interpreting, so 'infer' is correct.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word:
The award was given to ___ completed the project first — Raju or Meena?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Use WHO when it is the subject of a verb. In the embedded clause '___ completed the project first', the missing word is the subject of 'completed'. Rule: if you can substitute 'he/she', use 'who'; if 'him/her', use 'whom'. Here: 'she completed the project first' → use 'who'. Trap: 'To whom' is correct in 'to whom was it given' but not here, because the pronoun is the subject of the embedded clause, not the object.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word:
The school ___ believes in discipline, while its core ___ is to develop all-round students.
questions.explanation: A is correct. PRINCIPAL (noun/adj) = the head of a school; most important. PRINCIPLE (noun) = a fundamental rule or belief. Memory aid: 'The princIPAL is your PAL.' In this sentence: 'school principal' (head of school) and 'core principle' (fundamental belief). Trap: B reverses the two — 'principle believes' doesn't make grammatical or semantic sense since principles don't have beliefs.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word:
The cyclist remained ___ at the traffic light, while the teacher handed out ___ to the students.
questions.explanation: A is correct. STATIONARY (adjective) = not moving. STATIONERY (noun) = writing materials (paper, pens, etc.). Memory aid: stationERY → papER and pEn both have E. The cyclist not moving = stationary; writing materials given to students = stationery. SSC tests this pair regularly in sentence correction.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word:
Her blue scarf perfectly ___ed her blue eyes, and her colleague paid her a lovely ___ on it.
questions.explanation: B is correct. COMPLEMENT (verb/noun) = to complete or enhance; things that go well together (the scarf complements the eyes — they match). COMPLIMENT (verb/noun) = to praise or express admiration (the colleague paid a compliment = praised her). Memory aid: complEment = complete; complIment = I say nice things. So: 'scarf complemented eyes' (matched/enhanced) and 'paid a compliment' (praise).

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word:
The detective managed to ___ a confession through careful questioning, but the police later discovered the suspect had been involved in ___ activities.
questions.explanation: A is correct. ELICIT (verb) = to draw out or provoke a response (detective elicited a confession). ILLICIT (adjective) = not allowed by law or rules (illicit activities = unlawful). Memory aid: elIcit → Induce; iLLicit → iLLegal. Pronunciation trap: both sound similar (/ɪˈlɪsɪt/), making this a classic SSC confusable that appears in fill-in-the-blanks sections.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct word:
The spy was known for his ___ness — never revealing any information unnecessarily, whereas the classified project was kept ___ from the public.
questions.explanation: B is correct. DISCREET (adjective) = careful about not sharing sensitive information; tactful (spy's quality of not revealing info = discreet; discreetNESS is a valid noun form). DISCRETE (adjective) = individually separate and distinct (discrete components of a system). Memory aid: disCREET → keep it CREETED (secret); disCRETE → sEparaTEd (separate items). In this question: spy's personality trait = discreet; the project kept separate from public = discreet (hidden/secret).
